_comment: Discovery targets for `python -m scraper discover-all` — the automatic, scheduled
counterpart to the manual `discover` command. VERSION-CONTROLLED: treat it as code and
deploy it; do not hand-edit it on a server, or the next deploy will silently revert it.
Each entry expands to one (area, category) PAIR per category. A scheduled run takes the
next `--targets` pairs, ONE PER GROUP in round-robin order, so no pair is queried again
until every other pair in its group has had a turn.
`group` is the rotation bucket — island groups here. It exists so a national target list
spreads each run across Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao instead of draining the first group in
the file before the others are ever visited. The names are the FILE's vocabulary:
scraper/targets.py hardcodes none of them, so adding a group needs no Python change.
`area` is free text resolved by Nominatim (`--area`). `category` must be a word the active
provider knows — see CATEGORY_SELECTORS in scraper/providers/openstreetmap.py. These are
PROVIDER categories (OSM tags), deliberately NOT the CRM's Business Niche registry: the CRM
niche vocabulary is a separate business concern and must not leak into provider selectors.
Every pair below was validated with `discover --print-only --provider osm --limit 3` before
being added — each area resolves in Nominatim and each category returns businesses. Bacolod
City and Tagbilaran City were REJECTED by that check (car_repair returned 0); do not add a
city here without running the same check first.
`defaults.limit` bounds how many businesses a single pair may discover per run, and
`defaults.targets_per_run` how many pairs one run may touch. The volume ceiling is the product
of the two; both are clamped by MAX_LIMIT / MAX_TARGETS_PER_RUN in scraper/targets.py, which
exist to protect Overpass and Nominatim (shared community infrastructure) and must not be
raised to chase throughput. Widen coverage by ADDING TARGETS, not by lifting the caps.
Growth lever: the pool is meant to build continuously, so add areas/categories here rather
than increasing per-run volume. At 27 pairs and 3 targets per run the rotation completes in
9 nights — one pair per island group per night. More targets means a longer rotation, not a
bigger burst.
